case_name: Union of India and Another v Madhav S/O Gajanan Chaubal and Another
respondent:
Madhav S/O Gajanan Chaubal and Another
Supreme Court of India

18 September 1996
Civil Appeal No. 12871 of 1996
The Order of the Court was as follows :
Delay condoned.
Leave granted.
1.  On the last occasion where the matter had come up after notice, since the respondents were not represented either in person or through counsel and when, the counsel had pointed out the decision followed by the Tribunal, namely, Dr. Chakradhar Pasvan vs. State of Bihar [(1988) 2 SCC 214 1988 Indlaw SC 883], this Court had referred the matter to three-Judge Bench. Thus, the matter has come up today, Even now, none is appearing for the respondents; nor are they appearing in person. We have taken the assistance of Sri Goswami, learned senior counsel. We requested him to place on record the decisions for or against him. He has fairly argued case.
2.  The admitted facts are that in the National Savings Scheme Service the Government had created various posts upto the post of Super
facts: The admitted facts are that in the National Savings Scheme Service the Government had created various posts upto the post of Superintendent; there are number of posts but there is only one post of Secretary.
This post is a feeder post for promotion as Regional Deputy Director in which category there are several posts.
In the post of Secretary, point No.4 vacancy was reserved for Scheduled Tribes.

When that vacancy was sought to be filled up by promotion from the Superintendents in Group A category from Scheduled Tribe candidates, the respondent filed of in the Central Administrative Tribunal at Bombay.
issues: Whether the application of 40 point roster to the successive vacancies in the post of Secretary violates Article 16 (1) of the Constitution?
petitioner_arguments: He has taken us through various judgments of this Court concerning the question.

In General Manager, Southern, Southern Railway vs. Rangachari [(1962) 2 SCR 586 1961 Indlaw SC 148], the Constitution Bench, per majority, had held that appointment by reservation to the selection post was not violative of Article 16(1) of the Constitution.
The same principle was followed in the case of promotion in State of Kerala vs. Thomas [1976 1 SCR 1906 1975 Indlaw SC 52].
